sentences.text: Shri B.S. Gandhi, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Smt. Archana Kher, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.
Record of the trial Court be requisitioned.
Also heard on I.A. No.21241/2017; an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of petitioner Utkarsh Mittal.

The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner has been convicted for the offence under Section 7 (i) read with S.16 (i) (A) (i) and sentenced him to suffer six months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/- and under Section 7(i), 7 (v), 14 (A) read with S. 16 (i) (A) (i),
16 (i) (ii), 16 (ic) of prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced him to suffer six months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation vide impugned judgment dated 31.03.2016 passed by the JMFC-Sonkatch- District-Dewas in Criminal Case No.581/2009 and affirmed by the Appellate Court in Criminal Appeal No.186/2016.
The petitioner was on bail during trial and has not misused the liberty granted to him.
Disposal of the case is likely to take time.
Further, it is submitted that the petitioner is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the terms and conditions which may be imposed upon him by this Court.
Learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State argued in support of the impugned judgments and prays for rejection of the suspension application.
Looking to the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, application is allowed.

The execution of remaining jail sentence awarded to petitioner shall remain suspended during pendency of this criminal revision and he shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 10.01.2018 and on such further dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard.
